# Japan Rising: executable event specification — JX 1.1 ALPHA 2 R13.1

This catalogue is compiled into the installed event files. It lists every event, including technical receivers, cooldowns and verification. IDs and conditions below are generated from the same objects used by the build.

Total: 1822 events; 121 actionable decision entries. Counts include alternative paths and technical follow-ups; a campaign does not display them all.

## Cascade rules

- Investment: available decision -> paid pending project -> delayed completion -> exact reward, or refund if completion conditions fail. Delay reopens after 90 days; permanent dismissal never reopens.
- Country: defeat gate -> selected terms -> defeated country's withdrawal -> release/tag change -> puppet or neutral treaty -> owned-port transfer -> final-state check -> local defence. Japan does not issue a minor-country alliance-wide peace.
- Pacific armistice: two years at war -> qualifying position -> 180-day monitored hold -> American reply -> Japanese terms -> checked land transfers -> Allied-Pacific peace -> verification -> five-year treaty expiry.
- Soviet terms: deep Siberian objectives -> Soviet reply -> occupied-border transfer -> separate-bloc eastern peace -> optional Far Eastern client. Formal Axis membership blocks this limited peace.

## Exact events, gates and actions

### 28600001: Japan Rising - JX 1.1 ALPHA 2 R13.1

Country: JAP. Module: opening. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: False.

Japan enters 1933 with a powerful fleet, limited industrial resources and competing demands from the Army and Navy. Invest in factories, shipping, training and reserves to prepare for conflict in China and across the Pacific. Choose Japan's future alliances and peace terms from the position we build.

Garrisons defend local bases, Mountain Infantry handle difficult terrain and Marines lead opposed landings. Production priorities and regional agreements can support the forces you build.

### 28600005: The next industrial investment

Country: JAP. Module: industry. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Choose shipyard capacity or aircraft motor works. Shipyards add six IC after nine months. Aircraft works add four IC and cut aircraft construction by twelve days; they finish on the same timetable.

Funding costs 200 money and 900 supplies. Work takes 270 days. You can delay or dismiss this proposal even if you cannot fund it. ### 28600045: More room to repair the fleet

Country: JAP. Module: navy. Earliest year: 1938. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Tokyo and Hiroshima already have level-ten naval bases in this scenario. Build three naval-base levels at Kobe and three at Yokohama instead, spreading repair capacity across more ports. Or concentrate five levels and two AA levels at Kobe. Surviving ships still require reinforcement IC, supplies and time; sunk ships do not return.

Funding costs 200 money and 900 supplies. Work takes 240 days. You can delay or dismiss this proposal even if you cannot fund it. ### 28600103: A settlement for China

Country: JAP. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1937. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

China can no longer hold its main centres. A puppet joins Japan's wars and rebuilds local forces. A neutral treaty state stays outside our alliance and grants access.

A base treaty reserves only listed ports already held by Japan: Shanghai (1338). Other land returns to the local government. This settlement does not end Japan's other wars. Shanghai is the optional Japanese base. Other Chinese wars, including surviving Communist forces, are not silently settled.

Puppet terms also require 65 percent of Chinese victory points lost. An inherited army of 96 or more formations is reorganised into 96: 32 mobile now, 32 after one year and 32 after two years. A smaller army receives no free expansion. Locked formations remain local defenders.

### 28600112: China leaves its former alliance

Country: CHI. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

The government withdraws from its former alliance and accepts the Japanese settlement. ### 28600120: A settlement for India

Country: JAP. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

India can no longer hold its main centres. A puppet joins Japan's wars and rebuilds local forces. A neutral treaty state stays outside our alliance and grants access.

A base treaty reserves only listed ports already held by Japan: Bombay (1517). Other land returns to the local government. This settlement does not end Japan's other wars. Bombay is the optional Japanese base. Ordinary India starts as the British Raj; no Indian player-mod content is imported.

### 28600145: the Philippines leaves its former alliance

Country: PHI. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

The government withdraws from its former alliance and accepts the Japanese settlement. If the new national government already exists, a follow-up unites the defeated state with it instead of leaving a separate rump country. Otherwise the state changes its country identity. The agreed puppet or neutral relationship follows.


### 28600193: Sarawak leaves its former alliance

Country: SAR. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

The government withdraws from its former alliance and accepts the Japanese settlement. If the new national government already exists, a follow-up unites the defeated state with it instead of leaving a separate rump country. Otherwise the state changes its country identity. ### 28600322: Indonesia leaves its former alliance

Country: U05. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

### 28600330: A settlement for Vietnam

Country: JAP. Module: settlements. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Vietnam can no longer hold its main centres. A puppet joins Japan's wars and rebuilds local forces. A neutral treaty state stays outside our alliance and grants access.

### 28600478: America: the terms of defeat

Country: JAP. Module: usa. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

White peace returns occupied American land. Pacific terms concede US-owned Pacific islands. Overseas withdrawal adds strategic bases and ends listed aid and access agreements. The strongest terms add Alaska and eligible West Coast areas. California requires its whole map area; Oregon and Washington require the whole Washington area.

Only American-owned land in American or Japanese hands can be awarded. Other countries keep their property. Occupied US land outside the treaty returns under peace, including German occupations outside any agreed German concessions. America leaves its alliance wars; the surviving USA is not puppeted. Refusal allows another offer in 90 days.

Formal Axis entry shares Germany's existing alliance wars and changes which peace negotiations are possible. Japan can cooperate with Germany, send aid and fight a separate Soviet war without taking this step.

### 28600560: A limited peace with Nationalist China

Country: JAP. Module: china. Earliest year: 1937. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Japan holds Nanjing, Shanghai and Wuhan, and China has lost at least 35 percent of its national territory. A limited peace can end this war before the western capital falls.

China remains independent, keeps its surviving army and grants Japanese access. Japan retains Shanghai only if it is Chinese-owned and Japanese-held. Other occupied Chinese land returns to China. Communist and regional wars are separate. This closes neither a later war nor a later puppet settlement, but a two-year non-aggression treaty must be respected or explicitly broken.

### 28600566: A separate government in Guangxi

Country: JAP. Module: china. Earliest year: 1937. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: False.

Split Guangxi from the Chinese puppet into a smaller Japanese puppet. Only its listed homeland provinces owned by China will pass to it. Japan's bases and armies remain Japanese. The new state joins Japan's wars and grants access; China loses cores on the transferred regional land.

### 28600572: A separate government in Yunnan

Country: JAP. Module: china. Earliest year: 1937. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: False.

Split Yunnan from the Chinese puppet into a smaller Japanese puppet. Only its listed homeland provinces owned by China will pass to it. Japan's bases and armies remain Japanese. The new state joins Japan's wars and grants access; China loses cores on the transferred regional land.

This trades a larger unified Chinese economy for another local partner. Japan supplies 1,000 supplies and 100 money. You may instead keep China unified permanently. ### 28600583: Buy oil for a larger fleet

Country: JAP. Module: early. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Choose a two-year American fuel contract. The mixed contract buys 12 metal and 24 oil daily for 4 supplies and 1 money daily. The oil-first contract buys 48 oil daily for 6 supplies and 1.5 money daily. Either costs 80 money now. Delivery follows trade efficiency; embargo, war or expiry can end it. ### 28600645: Make the enemy fight for the island bases

Country: JAP. Module: activities. Earliest year: 1942. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Truk and Saipan are valuable bases, not self-defending symbols. Add two coastal-fort levels to each island, or add two airfield levels and two AA levels at Saipan. Coastal forts help against a landing; aircraft and ships still need to be assigned by you. Truk already has a level-ten airfield. Losing either island before completion returns the payment.

### 28601654: America accepts the terms of defeat

Country: JAP. Module: usa_invasion. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

The agreed American provinces have changed ownership and America is no longer at war with Japan. America has withdrawn from its alliance wars. Other countries retain their own wars. Put 21 small, local detachments on Taiwan, Okinawa, Amami and the Japanese Pacific islands. Each is capped at 25 percent of a full garrison division and has no artillery brigade. Mobilisation cannot expand it beyond that cap.

The call-up costs 53 manpower, 900 supplies and 60 money, once. These local defenders can resist an empty-base raid; they cannot replace a fleet or stop a supported invasion. The first local-defence call-up also transfers 180 convoy transports and 90 convoy escorts to the national shipping pool, once across all these call-ups. They support island supply; they are not troop-transport flotillas or combat destroyers. Route allocation remains under convoy management.

Country: JAP. Module: country_campaigns. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Any friendly treaty government can instead support a merchant contract: 160 convoy transports, 40 escorts and 4,000 Japanese supplies. Neutral terms remain neutral; no war is inherited by this programme.

### 28601739: Rural recovery: workshops or reserve rolls?

Country: JAP. Module: prewar_content. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Officials seek work for rural households while the Army wants a broader register of fit recruits. Industrial employment commits men who could otherwise enter the replacement pool. Reserve registration preserves that military option, but another levy is unpopular.

Employ the workforce in Nagoya workshops
Cost: 45 money, 400 supplies, 300 metal, 25 manpower.
Completion: 270 days. Nagoya gains 3 IC. Its 25-manpower civilian workforce is assigned when funding begins.

Register and train a larger national reserve
Cost: 45 money, 400 supplies, 300 metal.
Completion: 270 days. The national reserve gains 40 manpower. Dissent rises by 1.

Fund one proposal before the Pacific war or war with America or Britain. Work already under way may finish during war. Keep the named sites under Japanese control and supplied; if the work cannot proceed, the investment is returned.

### 28601742: The carrier safety commission

Country: JAP. Module: prewar_content. Earliest year: 1934. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

### 28601757: A foothold on the American mainland

Country: JAP. Module: us_campaign_content. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Japanese troops have taken San Diego, Los Angeles, San Francisco or Seattle while America still owns the port. Choose what the captured stores support: 3,500 supplies, or 1,500 supplies and 1,000 oil. These are captured stores; normal convoys must carry them forward and ordinary storage limits apply. America can organize a continental reserve response. Holding one port does not satisfy the existing national surrender or Pacific armistice requirements. This opening reward is paid once, including after a lost port is recaptured.

### 28601758: America calls a continental defence reserve

Country: USA. Module: us_campaign_content. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

A Japanese landing threatens the continental United States. Six reserve infantry divisions cost 78 American manpower and 2,400 supplies and require a safe American-owned, American-controlled staging city. Prefer Denver, Salt Lake City, Phoenix, then Kansas City. Use researched 1939 equipment, or researched 1936 equipment. If manpower, supplies, research or a safe city are missing, authorize one limited 40-manpower and 2,000-supply budget instead. This neither changes wars nor replaces the existing American army. Newly formed reserves enter at their allowed maximum strength; organisation follows ordinary deployment and later losses still apply.

### 28601759: America calls a continental defence reserve

Country: JAP. Module: us_campaign_content. Earliest year: 1933. Triggered receiver: True. Persistent: True.

American recruitment is responding to the invasion. If its budget and a safe staging city were available, six infantry divisions formed there, costing America 78 manpower and 2,400 supplies. Otherwise America authorized a limited 40-manpower and 2,000-supply budget instead; no formations were created. The divisions use the 1939 model only with American technology 1110, otherwise researched 1936 equipment. This response can occur once. Existing American forces remain in service.

### 28601764: The California corridor is in Japanese hands

Country: JAP. Module: us_campaign_content. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Japan holds San Diego, Los Angeles, Sacramento and San Francisco, at least 90 days after the first mainland landing. Connecting these centres makes captured stores usable as one limited campaign reserve. Choose 12,000 energy, 8,000 metal and 1,500 rares for industry, or 6,000 supplies and 1,500 oil for current operations. Stocks enter Japan's national pools and still need shipping; the cities remain with their legal owners. This is not an annexation or a peace settlement, and it awards nothing a second time.

### 28601765: America organizes a second continental reserve

Country: USA. Module: us_campaign_content. Earliest year: 1941. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

At least 60 days after the first landing, Japanese control of Las Vegas, Salt Lake City or Denver triggers a second and final six-division emergency reserve. It costs another 78 American manpower and 2,400 supplies, deploying only at American-owned and controlled Kansas City, Chicago or Washington. Researched 1939 infantry is preferred; researched 1936 infantry is the fallback. Missing resources, research or a safe city instead authorize one limited 40-manpower and 2,000-supply budget. No units appear in enemy territory. Newly formed reserves enter at their allowed maximum strength; organisation follows ordinary deployment and later losses still apply.

### 28601774: Type 93 Oxygen Torpedoes enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1935. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

The Type 93 oxygen torpedo gives eligible Japanese destroyers and cruisers a specialised surface-attack loadout. It uses an attachment slot and carries its normal ammunition and supply demand. The first two attachments enter the deployment pool, ready for eligible Japanese formations. They use the latest researched equipment whose service year has arrived. This first issue is already funded and recruited; it takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Additional attachments use normal production and operating costs.

### 28601776: Dokuritsu Konsei Mixed Brigade enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1937. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Independent mixed brigades combine infantry and supporting detachments for security and local defence. These are attachments for eligible land formations, not separate map divisions. The first two attachments enter the deployment pool, ready for eligible Japanese formations. They use the latest researched equipment whose service year has arrived. This first issue is already funded and recruited; it takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Additional attachments use normal production and operating costs.

### 28601778: Maritime Flying Boat Wing enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1938. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Large flying boats give Japan a long-range maritime search force. H6K equipment enters service from 1938; H8K equipment follows from 1942 when its research is complete. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home airfield. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.

### 28601780: Ka-Mi Naval Tank Detachment enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1942. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Ka-Mi naval tank detachments support eligible infantry and Marine assault formations. They still require oil and ordinary supply; they do not replace the assault division. The first two attachments enter the deployment pool, ready for eligible Japanese formations. They use the latest researched equipment whose service year has arrived. This first issue is already funded and recruited; it takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Additional attachments use normal production and operating costs.

### 28601782: Akizuki Anti-Air Escort Flotilla enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1942. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Akizuki-class escorts bring dedicated anti-aircraft cover to the fleet. They exchange some surface firepower for that role. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home port. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.

### 28601784: Teishin Airborne Division enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1942. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Teishin training begun in 1941 produces an airborne formation for service from 1942. Airborne missions still require transport aircraft and the normal mission conditions. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home airfield. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.

### 28601803: Expeditionary Assault Division enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1937. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

This expeditionary division combines full infantry strength with assault engineers and a lighter support train. It improves jungle, forest, river and urban operations while using fewer supplies, at the cost of some defence and anti-armour strength. This organisation is an alternative development for Japan. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home assembly area. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.

### 28601805: Long-Range Naval Attack Wing enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1938. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Long-range land-based naval bombers retain full naval striking power. They cost less to construct but use more fuel and are more vulnerable than standard naval bombers. Flying boats remain better maritime search aircraft. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home airfield. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.

### 28601807: Naval Long-Range Fighter Wing enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1940. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Land-based naval fighters extend air cover over distant approaches. They keep ordinary fighter firepower, with greater range but less speed and protection. They cannot be based on carriers. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home airfield. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.

### 28601809: Economical Escort Flotilla enters Japanese service

Country: JAP. Module: unique_unit_introductions. Earliest year: 1944. Triggered receiver: False. Persistent: True.

Matsu and Tachibana escorts put rapid replacement ahead of fleet speed and heavy torpedo armament. They are ordinary map flotillas for escort and anti-submarine operations, not convoy escort points. One initially recruited formation joins at an operational Japanese home port. Its equipment uses the latest researched model whose service year has arrived. The first formation is already funded and recruited: this issue takes no money, manpower or supplies from the national pool. Further formations require normal production, crews and maintenance. If no listed home base is usable, the issue waits until one is ready.
